Purpose This handbook introduces NimbusWorks Pvt. Ltd. ("the Company") to new and existing employees and sets out the general rules, expectations, and administrative processes that apply across all departments and locations. It is the **entry point** to the Company's policy framework. Where a specific topic has a dedicated policy, this handbook provides an overview and links to the authoritative document. Where no dedicated policy exists, this handbook is authoritative. This handbook does not create a contract of employment. Employment terms are governed by the individual employment agreement and applicable law. --- ## 2. Scope This handbook applies to: - All full-time employees - All part-time employees - All contract employees on engagements exceeding 90 calendar days - All interns (with additional rules per HR365-POL-012) - All office locations of NimbusWorks - All remote and hybrid work arrangements It does not apply to independent consultants or vendors, whose engagement is governed by their agreement. --- ## 3. Policy Statement NimbusWorks is committed to: - Providing a safe, inclusive, and professional workplace - Treating all employees with dignity and respect - Clear, transparent, and consistently applied rules - Fair and timely resolution of employee concerns - Supporting employee growth and wellbeing Employees are expected to: - Perform their duties with honesty, diligence, and professionalism - Respect colleagues, clients, and company property - Comply with Company policies and applicable law - Raise concerns promptly through the proper channels - Maintain confidentiality of Company and employee information This handbook is not a substitute for reading the underlying policies. Employees are responsible for knowing and complying with all applicable policies. --- ## 5. Company Overview ### 5.1 About NimbusWorks NimbusWorks Pvt. Ltd. is a technology company that builds and operates enterprise software for global clients. The Company is headquartered in India and operates across multiple locations with a distributed workforce. ### 5.2 Departments NimbusWorks is organized into five departments: | Department | Function | Led By | |---|---|---| | Engineering | Product development, infrastructure, quality | Engineering Head | | Product | Product strategy, design, program management | Product Head | | Sales & Marketing | Revenue generation, brand, customer acquisition | Sales & Marketing Head | | Finance & Operations | Finance, accounting, legal, facilities, IT | Finance & Operations Head | | Human Resources | Talent, culture, employee relations, policy | HR Head | Each Department Head reports to the CEO. ### 5.3 Locations - **Corporate Office:** Primary headquarters (address available on the HR365 portal) - **Branch Offices:** Additional locations as published -

Employment ### 6.1 Employment Types | Type | Definition | |---|---| | Full-Time | Standard 40-hour week (9-hour shift × 5 days, including breaks) | | Part-Time | Fewer hours per week, agreed contractually | | Contract | Fixed-term engagement exceeding 90 days | | Internship | Time-bound role, governed by HR365-POL-012 | ### 6.2 Employment Agreement Every employee has a written employment agreement that specifies: - Role and reporting line - Compensation - Working hours - Place of work - Notice period - Probation duration - Any special terms Any changes to employment terms are made via a written amendment. ### 6.3 Employee ID Every employee receives: - A unique Employee ID (used on the HR365 portal) - A company email address - An ID card (for on-site access) - Access credentials to internal systems Employees must carry their ID card on premises. Lost ID cards must be reported to IT within 24 hours. ### 6.4 Right to Work All employees must maintain valid documentation proving their legal right to work in their employment jurisdiction. HR verifies this at onboarding and periodically thereafter. --- ## 7. Probation and Onboarding ### 7.1 Probation Period - **Duration:** 90 calendar days from date of joining - **Extensions:** Up to 30 days, only with written notice and documented reason - **Termination during probation:** Either party may terminate with **7 days' written notice** - **Confirmation:** Communicated in writing by HR within **10 working days** after probation ends ### 7.2 Confirmation Confirmation is based on: - Performance during probation (as assessed by the manager) - Compliance with Company policies - Completion of required onboarding training - No active disciplinary action ### 7.3 Onboarding Checklist New hires must complete the following within the first week: 1. **ID card issuance** — collected from the IT desk on day 1 2. **IT account setup** — email, HR365 portal, VPN, and system access 3. **Benefits enrollment** — health insurance and other benefits per HR365-POL-006 4. **Mandatory orientation session** — HR-led, within the first week 5. **Policy acknowledgment** — sign-off on this handbook and related policies via the portal 6. **Respect at Workplace training** — completed within 30 days (see HR365-POL-005) 7. **IT Security briefing** — MFA setup and security awareness (see HR365-POL-008) 8. **Buddy assignment** — an experienced team member assigned as a point of contact ### 7.4 Buddy Program Every new hire is assigned a "buddy" — a peer in the same or adjacent team. The buddy's role: - Answer day-to-day questions - Introduce the team - Help navigate internal tools - Provide informal support during the first 90 days Buddies are not managers and are not responsible for the new hire's performance. ### 7.5 Probation Leave Restrictions During probation, employees are eligible only for: - Sick Leave (per HR365-POL-003) - Bereavement Leave (per HR365-POL-003) Other leave types become available on confirmation. --- ## 8. Pre-approved weekend or holiday work earns Comp-Off per HR365-POL-003, §7.7. ### 8.6 Flex Time Employees may request flexibility in start and end times with manager approval, provided: - Core hours are maintained - Total daily logged time meets the standard - Business needs are not affected --- ## 9. Professional Expectations ### 9.1 General Conduct Employees are expected to act with: - **Honesty** — truthful in communication, records, and reports - **Punctuality** — arriving on time for work, meetings, and commitments - **Respect** — toward colleagues, clients, vendors, and visitors - **Integrity** — declining to engage in unethical practices - **Accountability** — owning outcomes and learning from mistakes - **Collaboration** — supporting team goals over individual agendas ### 9.2 Communication Norms - **Responsiveness:** Reply to messages within 4 hours during working hours - **Channels:** Use company-approved tools (email, chat) for all work communication - **Meetings:** Arrive on time; cancel with reasonable notice if needed - **Documentation:** Record important decisions in writing - **Escalation:** Raise issues early via the manager ### 9.3 Dress Code - **Regular days:** Business casual (collared shirt, chinos, kurtas, sarees, or equivalent) - **Client-facing meetings:** Formal attire - **Office events:** As specified in the invite Employees should dress in a manner that is professional, comfortable, and respectful of the workplace. ### 9.4 Use of Company Resources Company resources (email, laptop, software, internet, printers) are provided for business purposes. - Incidental personal use is permitted within reason - Excessive personal use is not permitted - Use of company resources for illegal or unethical activity is prohibited - Company email may be monitored per the IT Security Policy (HR365-POL-008) ### 9.5 Conflicts of Interest Employees must disclose any situation that could create a conflict of interest, including: - Outside business interests that compete or intersect with NimbusWorks - Family or close personal relationships with vendors, clients, or other employees (where reporting lines intersect) - Personal investments in entities doing business with the Company - Board memberships or advisory roles outside the Company Disclosures are made via the HR365 Conflict Disclosure form. See HR365-POL-005 for full rules. ### 9.6 Confidentiality Employees must not disclose: - Company financial, strategic, or operational information - Client information - Employee personal information (unless authorized) - Trade secrets, source code, or intellectual property Obligations continue after employment ends. See HR365-POL-005, §4. --- ## 10. Updating Employee Information ### 11.1 Self-Service Portal Employees must update personal details via the HR365 ESS portal within **15 days** of any change. HR does not update records based on verbal requests alone. Details to keep current: - Residential address - Personal phone number - Emergency contact(s) - Bank account details - Nominee for insurance and PF - Marital status (for benefits updates) - Educational qualifications (for certain roles) - Passport details (for travel roles) ### 11.2 Verification Some updates require verification: - Bank account changes: verified against a cancelled cheque or bank statement - Address changes: verified against a utility bill or rental agreement (if address is used for tax purposes) - Nominee changes: requires signed nominee form ### 11.3 Failure to Update Failure to update records within the stated window may lead to: - Delay in payroll processing - Delay in benefits claims - Missed communications from HR - Rejection of certain claims (e.g., insurance claims for unlisted dependents) ### 11.4 HR Data Privacy HR handles employee data per the Company's privacy policy and applicable data protection laws. Employee data is not shared with third parties except as required for payroll, insurance, or legal compliance. --- ## 12. Communication Channels ### 12.1 Primary Channels | Channel | Purpose | |---|---| | Email | Formal communication, external communication | | Company chat (Slack/Teams equivalent) | Day-to-day work, quick questions | | HR365 portal | HR queries, leave, attendance, payroll, IT requests | | Video conferencing | Meetings, interviews, reviews | | Phone | Urgent matters | ### 12.2 Email Etiquette - Use clear subject lines - Keep messages concise and actionable - Reply to all when appropriate - Use "reply all" sparingly - Flag urgent items appropriately ### 12.3 Meetings - Schedule with clear purpose and agenda - Arrive on time - Cancel with reasonable notice if unavoidable - Record decisions in meeting minutes for recurring meetings - Keep meetings focused and within the scheduled duration ### 12.4 Response Times | Communication | Expected Response | |---|---| | Chat during working hours | Within 30 minutes | | Email (standard) | Within 4 hours | | Email (urgent, marked) | Within 1 hour | | HR ticket | Acknowledgment within 2 working days | ### 12.5 After-Hours Communication - Employees are not required to respond to messages outside their working hours - Managers should avoid messaging outside standard hours unless urgent - Any after-hours work earns Comp-Off only with pre-approval --- ## 13. Facilities and Amenities ### 13.1 Office Facilities - Designated workstations - Meeting rooms (bookable via the HR365 portal) - Cafeteria or pantry - Restrooms and wellness facilities - Recreation areas (where available) ### 13.2 Access Cards - ID cards are required for office access - Card sharing is prohibited - Lost cards must be reported within 24 hours ### 13.3 Clean Desk Policy - Sensitive documents must not be left on desks overnight - Lockable storage is provided for personal and sensitive items - Whiteboards and shared spaces must be cleared after use ### 13.4 Visitors - Visitors must register at reception - Visitors must be escorted by the host in office areas - Visitor badges must be returned at exit ### 13.5 Parking - Available on a first-come, first-served basis where provided - Reserved slots per department allocations ### 13.6 Sustainability - NimbusWorks encourages responsible use of resources - Print only when necessary - Dispose of waste in designated bins - Turn off equipment when not in use --- ## 14.

Learning and Development ### 14.1 Overview NimbusWorks supports continuous learning through: - Learning & Development Allowance (per HR365-POL-006) - Internal training programs - On-the-job mentoring - Sponsored certifications - Conference attendance ### 14.2 Learning & Development Allowance - **Amount:** Up to ₹20,000 per year - **Eligibility:** Confirmed employees - **What's covered:** Courses, certifications, conferences, and workshops relevant to the employee's current or planned role - **Approval:** Manager approval required for role relevance - **Claim:** Via the HR365 Finance portal ### 14.3 Internal Training - Mandatory training: Respect at Workplace (annual), IT Security (annual) - Optional training: Technical skills, leadership, soft skills, wellness - Attendance at mandatory training is tracked and non-compliance may be escalated ### 14.4 Performance and Career - Performance reviews are conducted periodically (frequency announced by HR) - Career development discussions occur at least once a year - Employees may apply for internal mobility postings on the HR365 portal --- ## 15. Compensation and Benefits Overview ### 15.1 Salary - Salary is processed monthly on the last working day - Payslips are published on the HR365 Finance portal by the 2nd working day of the following month - Full rules: HR365-POL-007 (Payroll Policy) ### 15.2 Benefits NimbusWorks provides: - Group Health Insurance (employee + up to 4 dependents) - Life Insurance - Meal Allowance - Internet Reimbursement - Learning & Development Allowance - Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Full details: HR365-POL-006 (Benefits Policy). ### 15.3 Reimbursements - Submit claims within 60 days of the expense - Attach valid documentation - Approval workflow varies by claim type - Approved claims are processed in the next payroll cycle ### 15.4 Tax Documents - Form 16 issued annually by June 15 - Investment declarations must be submitted by January 31 each year --- ## 16. Health, Safety, and Wellbeing ### 16.1 Workplace Safety NimbusWorks is committed to a safe workplace. Employees must: - Report safety hazards immediately (HR365 Safety Report form or Safety Officer) - Follow safety signage and protocols - Participate in emergency drills Full rules: HR365-POL-010 (Workplace Safety and Grievance Policy). ### 16.2 Emergency Procedures - **Fire:** Evacuate via designated exits; do not use elevators - **Medical:** Contact the on-site First Responder or call emergency services - **Security:** Report incidents to IT Security within 2 hours (see HR365-POL-008) - **Natural disaster:** Follow instructions from Safety Officers and local authorities ### 16.3 Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - Free, confidential counseling and support - Available 24×7 - Covers employee and immediate family - Use is entirely voluntary and confidential - Contact details available on the HR365 portal ### 16.4 Mental Health NimbusWorks recognizes mental health as integral to overall wellbeing. Support includes: - EAP counseling sessions - Mental health days (usable via Sick Leave per HR365-POL-003) - Flexible working arrangements (per HR365-POL-004) - Manager training on mental health awareness ### 16.5 Wellness Initiatives - Periodic wellness programs (yoga, fitness, mindfulness) - Ergonomic workstation setup - Health check-up camps (as announced) - Wellness allowance (where applicable per HR365-POL-006) --- ## 17. Grievance and Concerns ### 17.1 Raising Concerns Employees may raise concerns about: - Workplace conduct - Harassment or discrimination - Safety hazards - Policy violations - Compensation or leave matters - Manager relationships - Any other work-related issue ### 17.2 Channels | Concern | Channel | |---|---| | General workplace concerns | Direct manager, HR Helpdesk, or HR | | Harassment / discrimination | HR, Internal Committee, or Ethics Hotline | | Safety hazard | Safety Officer or HR365 Safety Report form | | Ethics / fraud | Anonymous Ethics Hotline | | Compensation | Payroll Helpdesk or HR | ### 17.3

Retaliation is a policy violation and grounds for disciplinary action. ### 17.5 Escalation Unresolved concerns may be escalated per the relevant policy (see HR365-POL-010 for grievance escalation). --- ## 18. Performance and Feedback ### 18.1 Performance Reviews Performance reviews are conducted periodically. Frequency and format are announced by HR. Reviews typically include: - Self-assessment - Manager assessment - Peer feedback (where applicable) - Goal setting for the next period ### 18.2 Continuous Feedback - Managers provide regular feedback throughout the year - Employees are encouraged to seek feedback proactively - Skip-level and peer feedback may be part of the review process ### 18.3 Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) If an employee's performance does not meet expectations: 1. Manager discusses specific concerns with the employee 2. A PIP is created with clear goals, timelines, and support 3. Duration: typically 30–90 days 4. Outcomes: improvement, role change, or separation as applicable ### 18.4 Recognition NimbusWorks recognizes high performance through: - Spot awards - Quarterly/Annual recognition - Internal nominations - Public acknowledgment in team meetings ### 18.5 Promotions - Promotion decisions are based on performance, capability, and business need - Typically assessed during annual review cycles - Changes in role, level, or compensation follow HR approval --- ## 19. Separation and Exit ### 19.1 Resignation - Submit a written resignation via the HR365 portal - Notice period: as per employment agreement (typically 30–90 days) - Shortened notice requires manager + HR approval ### 19.2 Termination The Company may terminate employment: - During probation: 7 days' written notice (per §7.1) - After confirmation: per employment agreement and applicable law - For cause (misconduct): process per HR365-POL-005 ### 19.3 Notice Period During notice period, employees must: - Continue to perform duties - Hand over responsibilities systematically - Not accept outside employment that conflicts with duties - Return all company property within 5 working days of last working day ### 19.4 Exit Checklist Before the last working day: 1. Hand over all projects and documentation 2. Return company laptop, monitor, headset, and other equipment 3. Return ID card and access cards 4. Complete exit interview with HR 5. Clear financial obligations (advances, reimbursements) 6. Sign final settlement acknowledgment ### 19.5 Final Settlement - Processed within **45 days** of the last working day - Includes salary up to last day, EL encashment (up to 30 days), and any statutory dues - Deductions for unpaid leave, unreturned equipment, or outstanding advances apply ### 19.6 Post-Employment Obligations - Confidentiality obligations continue indefinitely - Non-solicitation and non-compete clauses apply where specified in the employment agreement - Intellectual property created during employment belongs to the Company --- ## 20. Details are in your welcome email. **Q: Who is my manager?** A: Your reporting line is stated in your employment agreement and visible on the HR365 portal under your profile. **Q: What is a "buddy"?** A: A peer assigned to help you settle in during your first 90 days. Worked Scenarios ### Scenario 1: New Joiner's First Week **Day 1:** Collect ID card, complete IT setup, meet manager and buddy, HR orientation. **Day 2–3:** Shadow team members, complete mandatory training modules. **Day 4:** First team meeting, assigned initial tasks. **Day 5:** Check-in with manager, review of week 1. ### Scenario 2: Requesting a Flex Start **Employee:** Confirmed, personal commitments require a 10:30 AM start. **Correct approach:** Submit request to manager; if approved, adjust daily schedule to end at 7:30 PM. Core hours maintained. ### Scenario 3: Client Meeting Dress Code **Event:** Client-facing presentation. **Dress:** Formal business attire. **If unsure:** Ask the manager in advance. ### Scenario 4: Reporting a Safety Hazard **Event:** Employee notices a broken chair in the meeting room. **Correct approach:** Report via the HR365 Safety Report form or to the Safety Officer. Do not use the broken chair. ### Scenario 5: Conflict of Interest Disclosure **Event:** Employee's spouse is a vendor's account manager. **Correct approach:** Disclose via the HR365 Conflict Disclosure form. HR reviews and advises on management. ### Scenario 6: Harassment Report **Event:** Employee experiences inappropriate comments from a colleague. **Correct approach:** Report via HR, the Internal Committee, or the Ethics Hotline. Present, Half-Day, Absent, and Short-Day Definitions ### 6.1 Present An employee is marked Present if the total logged time for the day is **at least 8 hours** within the 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM window. - Breaks (lunch and short breaks) are counted within the 8 hours - Time before 8:00 AM and after 8:00 PM does not count toward the 8-hour threshold unless pre-approved by the manager - Multiple sessions within the day can be combined (e.g., check-in 9:00 AM, check-out 12:00 PM, check-in 1:00 PM, check-out 6:30 PM = 8.5 hours total) ### 6.2 Half-Day An employee is marked Half-Day if the total logged time for the day is **between 4 and 6 hours**. - 0.5 day is deducted from the leave balance (CL) or treated as LWP if no CL balance - Half-day requests must be pre-approved by the manager - Late arrivals that reduce logged time to under 6 hours may trigger an automatic half-day designation ### 6.3 Short Day An employee is marked Short Day if the total logged time for the day is **between 6 and 8 hours**. - 0.25 day is deducted from the leave balance (CL) or treated as LWP if no CL balance - Short Day is not an automatic manager designation — it's calculated by the system - Repeated Short Days may trigger manager discussion about workload or schedule ### 6.4 Absent An employee is marked Absent if: - Total logged time for the day is **less than 4 hours**, AND - No approved leave (SL, CL, EL, BL, etc.) covers the day, AND - No approved On Duty record exists Absent days are: - Deducted from payroll as LWP at the daily gross rate - Counted in the monthly absence report shared with managers - Escalated to HR if 2 or more unmarked absences occur in a single month ### 6.5 Week-Off and Holiday | Day Type | Attendance Required? Scope Applies to all employees on the NimbusWorks payroll, across all employment types (full-time, part-time, contract exceeding 90 days). ## 3. Definitions | Term | Definition | |---|---| | Payroll Cycle | The monthly period for which salary is processed | | Payroll Cutoff | The date (25th) after which attendance/leave changes apply to the next cycle | | Payslip | Monthly statement of gross pay, deductions, and net pay | | Gross Pay | Total earnings before deductions | | Net Pay | Amount credited after all deductions | | CTC | Cost to Company — total compensation including benefits | | PF | Provident Fund — statutory retirement contribution | | TDS | Tax Deducted at Source — income tax withheld monthly | | Form 16 | Annual tax certificate issued to employees | | Off-Cycle Payment | Payment outside the regular monthly cycle | | Final Settlement | Full and final dues processed on exit | ## 4. Payroll Cycle - Salary is processed **monthly** and credited on the **last working day** of each month - Attendance and leave records are **locked** on the **25th** of each month - Changes actioned after the 25th apply to the **following month's** cycle - If the last working day falls on a holiday or weekend, salary is credited on the preceding working day ## 5. Payslips - Published on the HR365 Finance portal by the **2nd working day** of the following month - Contents: - Gross pay (basic, HRA, allowances) - Deductions (PF, professional tax, TDS, LWP, other) - Net pay - Leave balance summary - Attendance summary (present, absent, LWP) - Payslips are retained on the portal for 7 years - Employees may download PDF copies for their records ## 6. Deductions ### 7.1 Statutory Deductions | Deduction | Basis | Rate | |---|---|---| | Provident Fund (PF) | Basic pay | 12% (employee contribution) | | Professional Tax | Per state slab | As applicable | | Income Tax (TDS) | As per declared tax regime | As per slab | ### 7.2 Other Deductions - **Unpaid Leave (LWP)** — daily gross rate × number of LWP days - **Notice recovery** — for short-notice exits - **Equipment recovery** — for unreturned or damaged equipment per HR365-POL-004 - **Loan repayment** — where applicable - **Salary advance recovery** — per agreed schedule ### 7.3 Daily Rate Calculation `Daily Gross Rate = Monthly Gross Salary / Number of Working Days in Month` Working days exclude weekends and Company holidays. ## 8. Tax Documents ### 8.1 Form 16 - Issued annually by **June 15** for the preceding financial year - Available for download on the HR365 Finance portal - Reflects TDS deducted and salary earned during the financial year ### 8.2 Investment Declarations - Must be submitted by **January 31** each year via the HR365 Finance portal - Applies to employees opting for the old tax regime - Declarations without supporting proof by the deadline may result in higher TDS in the final quarter ### 8.3 Proof Submission - Investment proofs must be uploaded by **February 15** - Missing or invalid proofs may result in TDS recovery in the following cycle ## 9. Purpose Defines how workplace safety concerns and grievances (including harassment complaints) are reported, investigated, and resolved at NimbusWorks. ## 2. Scope - **Safety:** All employees, contractors, and visitors to NimbusWorks premises - **Grievance:** All employees (including contractors where applicable) ## 3. Definitions | Term | Definition | |---|---| | Safety Hazard | Any condition that risks injury, illness, or property damage | | Grievance | A formal complaint about workplace conduct, decisions, or conditions | | Harassment | Unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic, or that creates a hostile environment | | Internal Committee (IC) | Committee constituted per applicable law for harassment matters | | Fact-Finding Review | Structured investigation into a grievance | | Need-to-Know | Principle of limiting information access to those who require it | | Anonymous Report | A complaint submitted without identifying the reporter | | Retaliation | Adverse action against a reporter or witness | | Escalation | Referral of an unresolved matter to a higher authority | ## 4. Safety Reporting ### 4.1 What to Report Any workplace safety hazard, including: - Fire risks (blocked exits, faulty wiring) - Electrical hazards - Structural issues - Ergonomic risks (poor seating, inadequate lighting) - Chemical or biological exposures - Slip, trip, and fall hazards - Violence or threat of violence - Any unsafe condition observed on premises ### 4.2 How to Report - **HR365 Safety Report form** (primary channel) - **Directly to the on-site Safety Officer** - Urgent safety risks must be reported **immediately** ### 4.3 Safety Officer Responsibilities - Conduct a facility walkthrough **monthly** - Log findings in the Safety Register - Ensure corrective actions are tracked to closure - Coordinate emergency drills - Maintain emergency contact lists ### 4.4 Safety Register - Maintained by the Safety Officer - Contains all reported hazards, actions taken, and status - Reviewed monthly by HR and department heads - Retained for 7 years ### 4.5 Emergency Procedures | Emergency | Action | |---|---| | Fire | Evacuate via designated exits; do not use elevators | | Medical | Contact on-site First Responder; call emergency services | | Security | Report to security and IT Security | | Natural disaster | Follow instructions from Safety Officers and local authorities | Emergency drills are conducted at least twice per year. ## 5. Harassment Reporting ### 5.1 What Constitutes Harassment - Unwelcome physical contact - Sexual advances or requests for favors - Verbal conduct (slurs, jokes, threats) based on protected characteristics - Non-verbal conduct (displaying offensive materials, gestures) - Quid pro quo conduct (implicit or explicit demands in return for benefits) - Any conduct creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment ### 5.2 Reporting Channels - **HR365 Grievance module** - **Directly with HR** - **Internal Committee (IC)** — for harassment matters per applicable law - **Anonymous Ethics Hotline** — where anonymity is preferred ### 5.3 Acknowledgment - Complaints are acknowledged within **2 working days** - Reporter is assigned a case reference number - Reporter is informed of next steps and timelines ### 5.4 Confidentiality All grievance and harassment matters are handled on a **strict need-to-know basis**. Non-Retaliation NimbusWorks prohibits retaliation against any employee who: - Reports a concern in good faith - Participates in an investigation - Supports a colleague in raising a concern Retaliation is itself grounds for disciplinary action, up to and including termination. ## 9. Anonymous Reports - Anonymous reports are accepted via the Ethics Hotline - Investigation proceeds to the extent possible without identifying the reporter - **Limitation:** Anonymous reports may restrict follow-up if the reporter cannot be contacted for clarification - Anonymous reports are logged and tracked to closure ## 10.
